**Original Question:**
I want to go to uni but i want the best one that is closest. According to The Guardian 2024 ranking, which is in the top 10 for English and has a career after 15 months rating of over 75 across all subjects? I also want the closest to Ashford (Kent) that has opportunities to study postgrad English

**Previous Reasoning Steps:**
[turn 1] We need to interpret question. User: "I want to go to uni but i want the best one that is closest. According to The Guardian 2024 ranking, which is in the top 10 for English and has a career after 15 months rating of over 75 across all subjects? I also want the closest to Ashford (Kent) that has opportunities to study postgrad English"

The Guardian 2024 ranking likely refers to The Guardian's "Top 10 universities per subject" lists? In 2024, The Guardian publication lists universities with "career prospects after 15 months" ratings. They also have a ranking of universities with career prospects. We need a university that

1. Is in the top 10 for English subjects in The Guardian 2024 ranking.

2. Has a career after 15 months rating of over 75 across all subjects. But "across all subjects" might refer to that university's rating for "career prospects after 15 months" for each subject? Or the rating overall? The Guardian provides a rating out of 100 for "career prospects after 15 months" for each university, presumably aggregated across all subjects. We need rating > 75.

3. Closest to Ashford, Kent. So among those that satisfy conditions, find the one that is geographically closest to Ashford.

4. The university must also offer postgraduate English study opportunities.

Thus we need to find among UK universities that tie, the nearest.

We need The Guardian ranking 2024. Let's search for Guardian 2024 ranking for English universities.

[turn 2] The Guardian University Guide 2024 is the relevant source. Need top 10 English subject universities. Also need career after 15 months rating over 75 across all subjects (I think Guardian ranks "Careers after 15 months" per subject). Must find universities in top 10 for English that have rating >75. Then find the closest to Ashford Kent. Also need opportunities to study postgraduate English.

We should find Guardian 2024 league table for English. Possibly find the table online. Let's search Guardian 2024 English ranking.

[turn 3] We need Guardian 2024 ranking: top 10 for English subject. Also career after 15 months rating >75 across all subjects? The Guardian ranking includes a "Career prospects (15 months)" score. We need universities whose English subject ranking is top 10, and whose overall Career after 15 months rating (maybe overall career prospects score?) is over 75. Then nearest to Ashford Kent. Also must offer postgraduate English opportunities.

Thus we need:

1. Guardian University Guide 2024 English subject league table top 10 list. 
2. Guardian overall career prospects rating – maybe "Career prospects (15 months)" score on national ranking, maybe after 15 months national average. Top universities with >75.

We might need to fetch the actual table.

Search for Guardian 2024 English ranking table.

Ashford is a town in the Ashford district, in the county of Kent, England. It lies on the River Great Stour at the southern or scarp edge of the North Downs, about 61 mi by road southeast of central London and 15 mi northwest of Folkestone by road. At the 2021 census, it had a population of 83,213. The name comes from the Old English... æscet, indicating a ford near a clump of ash trees. It has been a market town since the Middle Ages, and a regular market continues to be held.

The Romney, Hythe and Dymchurch Railway (RH&DR) is a gauge light railway in Kent, England, operating steam and internal combustion locomotives. The 13+1/2 mi line runs from the Cinque Port of Hythe via Dymchurch, St. Mary's Bay, New Romney and Romney Sands to Dungeness, close to the Dungeness nuclear power stations and Dungeness Lighthouse. The line is double track north of New Romney and single track south.

# Postgraduate Courses

Information about postgraduate study and the courses available in the English Department: MA Issues in Modern Culture, MA English Linguistics, and combined MPhil/PhD degrees.

As a postgraduate in UCL’s English Department you can expect:

*   To work with specialists in a wide range of fields.
*   A lively, engaged, and welcoming community of staff and students.
*   A full programme of research seminars, invited speakers, and papers given by graduate students, alongside research methods and career development workshops.
*   Access to an incomparable range of archives and libraries, including the Senate House Library and the British Library, both of which are nearby.

# Postgraduate Courses

Information about postgraduate study and the courses available in the English Department: MA Issues in Modern Culture, MA English Linguistics, and combined MPhil/PhD degrees.

As a postgraduate in UCL’s English Department you can expect:

*   To work with specialists in a wide range of fields.
*   A lively, engaged, and welcoming community of staff and students.
*   A full programme of research seminars, invited speakers, and papers given by graduate students, alongside research methods and career development workshops.
*   Access to an incomparable range of archives and libraries, including the Senate House Library and the British Library, both of which are nearby.

#### Things to do in London

![Image 13: London Eye](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/London-Eye-2009.JPG/250px-London-Eye-2009.JPG)
##### [London Eye(Opens in a new window)](https://www.rome2rio.com/redirects/attractions/?destinationUrl=http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Eye&provider=Wikipedia&language=en&currency=USD&requestId=01a0b340-fd2c-71e8-84a5-3d2c3d98650a&uid=USPor20260918064255916uzdd&label=ep01:f:a:m:d)

The London Eye, or the Millennium Wheel, is a cantilevered observation wheel on the South Bank of the River Thames in London. It is Europe's tallest cantilevered observation wheel, and the most popular paid tourist attraction in the United Kingdom with over three million visitors annually. It has been featured numerous times in popular culture. The structure is 135 m tall and the wheel has a diameter of 120 m. When it opened to the public in 2000 it was the world's tallest Ferris wheel. Its height was surpassed by the 160 m Star of Nanchang in 2006, the 165 m Singapore Flyer in 2008, the 167 m High Roller (Las Vegas) in 2014, and the 250 m Ain Dubai in 2021. Supported by an A-frame on one side only, unlike these taller examples, the Eye is described by its operators as "the world's tallest cantilevered observation wheel". The Eye offered the highest public viewing point in London until it was superseded by the 245 m observation deck on the 72nd floor of The Shard in early 2013.

London Museum of Water & Steam is an independent museum founded in 1975 as the Kew Bridge Steam Museum. It was rebranded in early 2014 following a major investment project.

![Image 15: Great Wheel](https://static.rome2rio.com/lp-proxy/assets/c790ac4b79e7075b8ec3bc4c0db80d7f6bff3ce0/amusement-BILFk2rt.png)
##### [Great Wheel(Opens in a new window)](https://www.rome2rio.com/redirects/attractions/?destinationUrl=http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Wheel&provider=Wikipedia&language=en&currency=USD&requestId=01a0b340-fd2c-71e8-84a5-3d2c3d98650a&uid=USPor20260918064255916uzdd&label=ep01:f:a:m:d)

The Great Wheel, also known as the Gigantic Wheel, or Graydon Wheel, was built for the Empire of India Exhibition at Earls Court, London, in the United Kingdom. Construction began in March 1894 at the works of Maudslay, Sons and Field in Greenwich and it opened to the public on 17 July 1895. Modelled on the original Ferris Wheel which featured at the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago, US, it was 308 ft tall and 82.3 m in diameter. and weighed about 900 tons. It stayed in service until 1906, by which time its 40 cars (each with a capacity of 30 persons) had carried over 2.5 million passengers. It was demolished in 1907 following its last use with the Imperial Austrian Exhibition of 1906 as it was no longer profitable to run.

##### [Chessington World of Adventures(Opens in a new window)](https://www.rome2rio.com/redirects/attractions/?destinationUrl=http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chessington_World_of_Adventures&provider=Wikipedia&language=en&currency=USD&requestId=01a0b340-fd2c-71e8-84a5-3d2c3d98650a&uid=USPor20260918064255916uzdd&label=ep01:f:a:m:d)

Chessington World of Adventures Resort is a 128 acre theme park, zoo and hotel complex in Chessington, Greater London, England, around 12 mi southwest of Central London. The complex originally opened as Chessington Zoo in 1931; the theme park aspect was developed by The Tussauds Group, debuting on 7 July 1987 as one of the first combined animal-amusement parks in the UK. The theme park, which features over 40 rides, is now owned by Merlin Entertainments, following its merger with The Tussauds Group in 2007. Under Merlin, Chessington has been increasingly developed into a resort and tourist destination, including two on-site hotels, swimming pools, a campground, spa and fitness facilities.

### ![Image 12: London, United Kingdom](https://static.rome2rio.com/lp-proxy/assets/c790ac4b79e7075b8ec3bc4c0db80d7f6bff3ce0/gb-DzL3D2da.png)[London(opens in a new window)](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/London),[United Kingdom(opens in a new window)](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/United-Kingdom)

One of the most popular tourist destinations in the world, London is a traveller’s delight. Catering to a wide range of tastes, there’s something for everyone in the English capital. London boasts myriad historical sites, art galleries, sporting attractions, world-class restaurants and eateries, high fashion outlets, and cultural events. Take a... cruise down the iconic River Thames, visit iconic Big Ben and the Tower of London, say hi to the Queen at Buckingham Palace, catch a show at a famous West End theatre or be one with nature in much-loved Hyde Park or Kensington Gardens.

#### Things to do in London

![Image 13: London Eye](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/London-Eye-2009.JPG/250px-London-Eye-2009.JPG)
##### [London Eye(Opens in a new window)](https://www.rome2rio.com/redirects/attractions/?destinationUrl=http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Eye&provider=Wikipedia&language=en&currency=USD&requestId=01a0b340-fd2c-71e8-84a5-3d2c3d98650a&uid=USPor20260918064255916uzdd&label=ep01:f:a:m:d)

The London Eye, or the Millennium Wheel, is a cantilevered observation wheel on the South Bank of the River Thames in London. It is Europe's tallest cantilevered observation wheel, and the most popular paid tourist attraction in the United Kingdom with over three million visitors annually. It has been featured numerous times in popular culture. The structure is 135 m tall and the wheel has a diameter of 120 m. When it opened to the public in 2000 it was the world's tallest Ferris wheel. Its height was surpassed by the 160 m Star of Nanchang in 2006, the 165 m Singapore Flyer in 2008, the 167 m High Roller (Las Vegas) in 2014, and the 250 m Ain Dubai in 2021. Supported by an A-frame on one side only, unlike these taller examples, the Eye is described by its operators as "the world's tallest cantilevered observation wheel". The Eye offered the highest public viewing point in London until it was superseded by the 245 m observation deck on the 72nd floor of The Shard in early 2013.

![Image 14: London Museum of Water & Steam](https://farm1.staticflickr.com/43/74796320_e6cad472d1_n.jpg)
##### [London Museum of Water & Steam(Opens in a new window)](https://www.rome2rio.com/redirects/attractions/?destinationUrl=http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Museum_of_Water_&_Steam&provider=Wikipedia&language=en&currency=USD&requestId=01a0b340-fd2c-71e8-84a5-3d2c3d98650a&uid=USPor20260918064255916uzdd&label=ep01:f:a:m:d)

London Museum of Water & Steam is an independent museum founded in 1975 as the Kew Bridge Steam Museum. It was rebranded in early 2014 following a major investment project.

![Image 15: Great Wheel](https://static.rome2rio.com/lp-proxy/assets/c790ac4b79e7075b8ec3bc4c0db80d7f6bff3ce0/amusement-BILFk2rt.png)
##### [Great Wheel(Opens in a new window)](https://www.rome2rio.com/redirects/attractions/?destinationUrl=http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Wheel&provider=Wikipedia&language=en&currency=USD&requestId=01a0b340-fd2c-71e8-84a5-3d2c3d98650a&uid=USPor20260918064255916uzdd&label=ep01:f:a:m:d)

The Great Wheel, also known as the Gigantic Wheel, or Graydon Wheel, was built for the Empire of India Exhibition at Earls Court, London, in the United Kingdom. Construction began in March 1894 at the works of Maudslay, Sons and Field in Greenwich and it opened to the public on 17 July 1895. Modelled on the original Ferris Wheel which featured at the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago, US, it was 308 ft tall and 82.3 m in diameter. and weighed about 900 tons. It stayed in service until 1906, by which time its 40 cars (each with a capacity of 30 persons) had carried over 2.5 million passengers. It was demolished in 1907 following its last use with the Imperial Austrian Exhibition of 1906 as it was no longer profitable to run.

![Image 16: Chessington World of Adventures](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/b/b6/CWOAR_Logo.png/250px-CWOAR_Logo.png)
##### [Chessington World of Adventures(Opens in a new window)](https://www.rome2rio.com/redirects/attractions/?destinationUrl=http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chessington_World_of_Adventures&provider=Wikipedia&language=en&currency=USD&requestId=01a0b340-fd2c-71e8-84a5-3d2c3d98650a&uid=USPor20260918064255916uzdd&label=ep01:f:a:m:d)

Chessington World of Adventures Resort is a 128 acre theme park, zoo and hotel complex in Chessington, Greater London, England, around 12 mi southwest of Central London. The complex originally opened as Chessington Zoo in 1931; the theme park aspect was developed by The Tussauds Group, debuting on 7 July 1987 as one of the first combined animal-amusement parks in the UK. The theme park, which features over 40 rides, is now owned by Merlin Entertainments, following its merger with The Tussauds Group in 2007. Under Merlin, Chessington has been increasingly developed into a resort and tourist destination, including two on-site hotels, swimming pools, a campground, spa and fitness facilities.
